meta: Why are some tiny models, small enough to run on a phone, still pretty smart? One secret is distillation: a big model is the teacher, answering lots of questions, and a small model learns from it.
thu: Next time you pick a model in an AI app, try the mini or fast version for small tasks like summarizing or rewriting a sentence. Compare and see whether the results differ much.

muc.title: Small but smart?
muc.text: Mark wonders why some tiny models, small enough to run on a phone, are still pretty smart.

muc.title: A big teacher, a small student
muc.text: One secret is distillation. A big model is the teacher, answering lots and lots of questions. A small model is the student, learning from how the teacher answers.

muc.title: Learning the hesitation too
muc.text: The student doesn't just learn the right answer. It also learns how much the teacher hesitated between answers. That information helps the student learn much faster.

muc.title: Small, fast, cheap
muc.text: The result is a small, fast, cheap model that keeps most of the teacher's skill, especially at the tasks it was taught.

muc.title: When you see this word
muc.text: When you see this word, think: a small model learning from a big one. That's why there are fast, cheap mini versions, as in video 18.
